label: Aquinas on self-willing, necessary means and voluntary production
summary: ST I q.19 a.3 distinguishes absolute and suppositional necessity and restricts necessary willing of means to indispensable means of the willed end. Q.19 a.4 explains God's effect production by intellect and will. Its second reason invokes uniform natural action unless impeded, then applies divine unlimited perfection in the particular case. It gives no criterion that arbitrary same-set-up modal variation makes a producing power rational. A stochastic non-rational propensity is the specific alternative the existing will-versus-chance inquiry tests. Follow-up (2026-11-26). I q.19 a.10's alternative of willing a thing to be or not to be concerns the agent already identified as God with will. The modal alternatives are consequences of that account, so the argument cannot infer rationality from arbitrary variation alone. A.8 additionally distinguishes the disposition of secondary causes from the first agent’s willing.
blocker: To test 6e4b519b, justify why the actual domain excludes non-rational stochastic variation with the same setup. Neither the divine free-choice case nor secondary contingency answers that exclusion.
